title: Epochal batch quietude: slot lockups, priority inversion and remediation playbook
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-19 we observed repeated multi-minute periods where continuous batch formation across a subset of serving pods dropped to near-zero ('quietude'), producing tail latency spikes for latency-sensitive customers and an apparent unfairness where lower-priority tenants consumed disproportionate slots after the quiet window. This ticket captures the incident drive, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and a concrete playbook of action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-19T09:12Z - First alert: per-pod batch-formation-rate graph on dashboard showed 90% reduction for pod-group us-east-1a-serve-62
2026-02-19T09:15Z - Pager triggered; ops started investigating runtime/serving metrics and request traces
2026-02-19T09:22Z - Observed client retry amplification from certain customers coincident with long-tail latency increase; KV cache miss spikes aligned with quiet window start
2026-02-19T09:33Z - Team rolled temporary scheduler soft-cap to prevent single-tenant monopolization; partial recovery observed
2026-02-19T09:50Z - Deployed emergency patch to revert a recent priority-weight change in runtime-1.23 and enabled fairness mode on affected node pool
2026-02-19T10:05Z - Service returned to baseline batch formation rates; monitoring kept under heightened alert for 24 hours
2026-02-20 - Post-incident working session to triage root causes and draft long-term fixes
root_cause: A recent change in the scheduler weight calculation (runtime-1.23) introduced an integer truncation when converting floating tenant weights to slot quotas under low-window occupancy. Under a specific request shape (many short requests with high KV cache miss variance), the truncation caused repeated lockups on scheduler slot allocation. This produced a batch quietude window where the scheduler withheld forming batches while waiting for locked slots to be released. Meanwhile, client-side retries and backpressure propagated, causing certain tenants with edge-case weight configurations to get disproportionate wake-up priority once locks released, creating the perceived unfairness.
mitigations: Immediate rollback of the weight truncation change in runtime-1.23 (hotfix deployed 2026-02-19 09:50Z)
Enabled per-pool fairness-mode that enforces min-slot guarantees for multi-tenant pools
Applied a soft cap on consecutive slots allocated to a single tenant (config change) to reduce monopolization while we implement stronger fixes
Increased alerting granularity: batch-formation-rate per pod, per-tenant slot-hold-time, and KV-cache-miss correlation graphs
action_items: ENG-SCHED-1: Replace truncation logic with saturating float-to-int conversion and add unit tests for boundary weights (owner: Marcus Lin, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-01)
ENG-SCHED-2: Implement per-tenant slot-timeout that force-releases locks after N ms to avoid indefinite quiet windows (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-MON-1: Add synthetic e2e test that simulates short-request bursts with KV-miss variance to exercise scheduler under production load shapes (owner: Dalia Park, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-08)
ENG-RPC-1: Harden client retry jitter and add server-side retry suppression flag to break retry amplification cycles (owner: Tomas Rivera, estimate: 4, due: 2026-04-01)

ENG-OBS-1: Create dashboard pane correlating per-tenant request rate, slot allocation, KV cache hitrate, and client retries for faster root cause identification (owner: Marcus Lin, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-05)
ENG-RUNBOOK-1: Update batcher incident runbook with a dedicated 'quietude' play section including detection queries and immediate config toggles (owner: Aisha Gomez, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-03)
ENG-PERM-1: Schedule an automated canary for every scheduler change that runs the synthetic e2e test before merge to mainline (owner: Platform CI team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-SEC-1: Review weight-as-config semantics with Security for potential edge-case misconfigurations that could be exploited for denial-of-service (owner: Zoe Martin, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-DOC-1: Publish a changelog note for runtime-1.23 documenting the rollback and the reasoning to keep customer-facing transparency (owner: Marketing eng-comm, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-06)
followups: Validate fix under bursty traffic using load generator in staging (status: planned)
Run an internal retrospective focused on scheduling invariants and numeric stability in weight math
Coordinate with Solutions Eng to notify customers who saw elevated latency and document mitigations available via dedicated pools
Track related fairness metrics for 30 days after deploying the forced-release timeout to ensure no regression
